name: Gurindji
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Ennever, Thomas, Felicity Meakins & Erich R. Round. 2017. A replicable acoustic measure of lenition and the nature of variability in Gurindji stops. Laboratory Phonology: Journal of the Association for Laboratory Phonology 8(1): 20, pp. 1-32. doi:10.5334/labphon.18 (CC BY; publisher galley PDF via the Internet Archive, saved)
catalog_locator: sec. 1.1.2 'Morphological and prosodic structure', p. 3 (Art. 20, page 3 of 32); hedge on stress assignment in sec. 6.1 Discussion, p. 24
catalog_quote: Primary stress falls on the initial syllable of Gurindji words without exception. The stress system has not been studied in detail, though broadly speaking, it resembles those of many Pama-Nyungan languages, with secondary stress on most suffix-initial syllables and alternating stress otherwise (Dixon, 2002, p. 557). A consequence is that word-initial syllables fall at the left boundaries of both the morphosyntactic word and a prosodic word. ... Given the state of knowledge of Gurindji’s stress system, we make no specific claims about foot boundaries, other than to note that word-initial tokens will always be foot-initial also. [sec. 6.1, p. 24] Importantly though, we did not distinguish post-tonic consonants from other medial consonants, nor do we have a satisfactory account of stress assignment. ... Further discussion of the interplay between stress, consonant lengthening, and lenition effects awaits more careful prosodic analyses of Gurindji.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress is fixed on the first syllable of the word, exceptionless; secondary stresses fall on the initial syllables of (most) suffixes and otherwise alternate; the authors state the system beyond primary stress has not been studied in detail.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on most suffix-initial syllables, alternating stress otherwise (impressionistic, with reference to Dixon 2002:557); p. 24 adds 'nor do we have a satisfactory account of stress assignment' and that post-tonic consonants were not distinguished.
new_statements.exceptions: None for primary stress ('without exception'); secondary-stress placement hedged ('most suffix-initial syllables').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (morphosyntactic word = left edge of prosodic word); statement made as background to a casual-speech corpus study of Gurindji spoken at Kalkaringi, co-authored by the grammar's first author (Meakins).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Gurindji proper (traditional Gurindji of Kalkaringi/Daguragu, NT; guri1247, ISO gue), not the mixed language Gurindji Kriol (guri1249), which is already in the catalog from Meakins 2013 APiCS.
